headline: Diagnostics volume and pricing lift margins, profit growth
summary_short: IDEXX reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.22B, up 9.7% y/y and 6.6% q/q, with diluted EPS of $4.27, up 17.6% y/y on margin expansion and continued buybacks.
summary_long: Revenue rose 6.6% q/q and 9.7% y/y to $1.22B on higher CAG Diagnostics recurring volumes and realized pricing, partly offset by fewer IDEXX inVue Dx instrument placements versus last year's launch quarter. Gross margin expanded 140bp y/y on volume mix, productivity, and net pricing, lifting gross profit 12.1% y/y to $779.1M. Operating income rose 14.1% y/y to $425.6M despite higher personnel and technology-investment costs; diluted EPS grew 17.6% y/y to $4.27, aided by $332.3M of buybacks this quarter. Cash was $196.9M, up from $180.1M at year-end, after $121.0M of net Credit Facility borrowings. Management maintained its roughly $180M FY2026 capital-expenditure plan.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by higher CAG Diagnostics recurring volumes (VetLab consumables, reference-lab testing) and higher realized prices; partly offset by fewer IDEXX inVue Dx instrument placements versus Q2 2025's broad launch quarter.
140bp y/y margin expansion from higher-margin diagnostics/lab volume mix, lower premium-instrument mix, productivity gains, and net price realization, which offset inflationary costs.
Opex grew on higher personnel, travel, and commercial-expansion costs plus higher depreciation on technology/infrastructure investment, but revenue and margin gains outpaced the increase.
EPS growth reflects higher operating income plus a lower diluted share count from continued buybacks; the release does not decompose the exact split between the two.
Release attributes the quarter to durable CAG Diagnostics volume and pricing strength plus margin execution, with instrument comps normalizing after last year's inVue Dx launch surge.
